topic: 生活方式与观点支持 · Independent new scenario: comparing environmental monitoring methods
grammarFocus: 原因、结果与让步从句；may / might / can 的语气差别。 Teach the new rule in Chinese, then provide at least 8 distinct grammar questions in new sentences. Distinguish a newly taught form from revision. All main reading/listening question prompts and options must be English, with short A0/A1 English prompts. Chinese explanations are allowed. Preserve a coherent new scenario; do not rename an earlier text, reuse its facts or reveal answers in question stems.
sourcePolicy: Project-original scenario; simulated figures and people; no copied official test, textbook, GitHub PDF or third-party audio.
title: Comparing Environmental Monitoring Methods: A Community Air-Quality Project
instructions: 阅读一篇关于社区空气质量监测的短文，完成10道阅读理解题（单选、填空、匹配、判断正误/未提及）。然后学习语法：原因、结果与让步从句，以及 may / might / can 的语气差别。所有题目和选项均为英文，解释为中文。本材料为模拟教学材料，不是官方雅思考试，也不代表任何官方分数。
passage:
A Community Air-Quality Project

[A] Last spring, the Greenfield Community Centre started a small air-quality project. The centre is near a busy road and a new building site. Many families wanted to know if the air was safe for children. The project leader, Ms. Chen, said, "We cannot test every street, so we must choose our methods carefully." The team compared three ways to monitor air quality: low-cost sensors, official monitoring stations, and simple dust traps.

[B] Low-cost sensors are small boxes that people can put on a balcony or a window. They are cheap, and they send data every minute. However, because they are cheap, they may not be very accurate. Ms. Chen explained, "The sensor is useful for showing changes during the day, but it might give a wrong number when the air is very wet." The team decided to use sensors in ten homes near the road. They put the sensors at the same height, so the results could be compared fairly.

[C] Official monitoring stations are large and expensive. They are very accurate, but there are only two stations in the whole town. One station is near the park, and the other is near the train station. Neither station is close to the new building site. Therefore, the team could not use station data to answer questions about the building site. Ms. Chen said, "Although the stations are excellent, they cannot tell us about our street."

[D] Simple dust traps are the third method. A dust trap is a box with a sticky surface. Dust sticks to the surface, and after one week, the team can see how much dust is in the air. Dust traps are very cheap, and anyone can make one. However, they only show the total dust for a week. They cannot show when the dust was high or low. The team used dust traps in five places: two near the road, two near the building site, and one in the community garden.

[E] After eight weeks, the team compared the results. The sensors showed that dust was highest between 7 and 9 in the morning, when many cars use the road. The dust traps near the building site were very dirty, but the trap in the garden was quite clean. The official station near the park showed low dust all month. Ms. Chen said, "Because the station is far from the road, its data does not describe our problem."

[F] The team also asked the families about the smell and noise. Some families said the air smelled bad in the evening. Others said they did not notice anything. Ms. Chen reminded everyone, "We may not have perfect data, but we can still take action. We can ask the town to water the building site road, and we can plant more trees near the school." The project report will go to the town council next month. The team hopes the council will support a second project with more sensors next year.

questions.prompt: Why did the Greenfield Community Centre start the project?
options: To test every street in the town
To know if the air was safe for children
To sell low-cost sensors to families
To build a new road near the school
answers: To know if the air was safe for children
questions.explanation: 第一段明确说许多家庭想知道空气对孩子是否安全，因此项目启动。
questions.evidence: Many families wanted to know if the air was safe for children.

questions.prompt: What is one problem with low-cost sensors?
options: They are too expensive for families.
They may not be very accurate.
They cannot send data every minute.
They are too large for a balcony.
answers: They may not be very accurate.
questions.explanation: 第二段说传感器便宜，但可能不太准确。
questions.evidence: However, because they are cheap, they may not be very accurate.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with ONE WORD from the passage: The team put the sensors at the same ______, so the results could be compared fairly.
questions.explanation: 第二段最后一句说团队把传感器放在同一高度。
questions.evidence: They put the sensors at the same height, so the results could be compared fairly.

questions.prompt: Why could the team NOT use official station data for the building site?
options: The stations were too expensive to use.
Neither station was close to the new building site.
The stations only worked in the park.
The stations were closed for eight weeks.
answers: Neither station was close to the new building site.
questions.explanation: 第三段说两个官方站都不靠近新建筑工地，因此不能回答工地的问题。
questions.evidence: Neither station is close to the new building site.

questions.prompt: What is one limitation of dust traps?
options: They only show the total dust for a week.
They cannot be made by anyone.
answers: They only show the total dust for a week.
questions.explanation: 第四段说灰尘收集器只显示一周的总灰尘量，不能显示何时高何时低。
questions.evidence: However, they only show the total dust for a week.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with ONE WORD from the passage: The sensors showed that dust was highest between 7 and 9 in the ______.
questions.explanation: 第五段说传感器显示早上7点到9点灰尘最高。
questions.evidence: The sensors showed that dust was highest between 7 and 9 in the morning, when many cars use the road.

options: A cheap method with a simple weekly result
The most accurate station in town
How to plant trees near the school
Why families did not notice the smell
answers: A cheap method with a simple weekly result
questions.explanation: 第四段介绍灰尘收集器便宜、简单，但只给出一周的总量，因此标题应为“便宜方法，简单周结果”。
questions.evidence: Dust traps are very cheap, and anyone can make one. However, they only show the total dust for a week.

questions.prompt: True, False, or Not Given: The official station near the park showed high dust all month.
questions.explanation: 第五段明确说公园附近的官方站整月显示低灰尘，与题干“高灰尘”矛盾，因此为 False。
questions.evidence: The official station near the park showed low dust all month.

questions.prompt: True, False, or Not Given: The team asked the families about the smell and noise.
questions.explanation: 第六段第一句明确说团队询问了家庭关于气味和噪音的情况。
questions.evidence: The team also asked the families about the smell and noise.

questions.prompt: True, False, or Not Given: The town council has already approved the second project.
questions.explanation: 文中只说报告下个月提交给镇议会，团队希望议会支持明年的第二个项目，但并未说明议会是否已经批准。所需事实“议会已批准”在文中缺失，因此为 Not Given。
questions.evidence: The project report will go to the town council next month. The team hopes the council will support a second project with more sensors next year.

grammar.title: 原因、结果与让步从句；may / might / can 的语气差别
grammar.explanation: 英语中，原因从句常用 because / since / as 引导，说明“为什么”；结果常用 so / therefore 引出“所以”；让步从句常用 although / though / even though 引导，表示“虽然……但是……”。注意：although 不能和 but 同时使用；because 不能和 so 同时使用。情态动词 may / might / can 都表示“可能/能够”，但语气不同：can 表示一般能力或客观可能；may 表示较有把握的推测或允许；might 表示把握更小的推测。例如：The sensor can send data every minute.（能力）It may rain later.（较有把握）It might be wrong.（把握较小）。
grammar.example: However, because they are cheap, they may not be very accurate.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: ______ they are cheap, they may not be very accurate.
questions.explanation: 句子前后是因果关系：因为便宜，所以可能不准确。Because 引导原因从句。
questions.evidence: However, because they are cheap, they may not be very accurate.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: The station is far from the road, ______ its data does not describe our problem.
questions.explanation: 前句是原因，后句是结果，用 so 引出结果。
questions.evidence: Because the station is far from the road, its data does not describe our problem.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: ______ the stations are excellent, they cannot tell us about our street.
questions.explanation: 前后是让步关系：虽然站很好，但不能告诉我们街道的情况。Although 引导让步从句。
questions.evidence: Although the stations are excellent, they cannot tell us about our street.

options: Although the trap is cheap, but it only shows weekly dust.
Although the trap is cheap, it only shows weekly dust.
Because the trap is cheap, so it only shows weekly dust.
The trap is cheap, although it only shows weekly dust.
answers: Although the trap is cheap, it only shows weekly dust.
questions.explanation: although 不能与 but 连用；because 不能与 so 连用。只有第二句正确。
questions.evidence: Dust traps are very cheap, and anyone can make one. However, they only show the total dust for a week.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word: The sensor ______ send data every minute. (ability)
questions.evidence: They are cheap, and they send data every minute.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word: The air ______ be wet tomorrow, so the sensor might give a wrong number. (small possibility)
questions.explanation: 表示把握较小的推测用 might。
questions.evidence: The sensor is useful for showing changes during the day, but it might give a wrong number when the air is very wet.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word: We ______ not have perfect data, but we can still take action. (possibility)
questions.explanation: 表示“可能没有完美数据”，用 may 表示较有把握的推测。
questions.evidence: We may not have perfect data, but we can still take action.

options: Because the road is busy, so the dust is high.
Although the road is busy, but the dust is high.
Because the road is busy, the dust is high.
The road is busy, because so the dust is high.
answers: Because the road is busy, the dust is high.
questions.explanation: because 引导原因从句，主句前不再加 so；although 不与 but 连用。第三句正确。
questions.evidence: The sensors showed that dust was highest between 7 and 9 in the morning, when many cars use the road.

part1: Do you often check the air quality in your city?
What do you do when the air is bad?
Do you prefer to walk or take a bus? Why?
Is there a park near your home?
speaking.part2: Describe a time when you compared two ways to do something. You should say: what you compared; why you compared them; what the result was; and explain what you learned from the comparison.
part3: Why might people use cheap sensors instead of official stations?
What can governments do to improve air quality?
Do you think people can take action even without perfect data?
How might technology change environmental monitoring in the future?

transfer.writing: Write a short report (120–150 words) for your community centre. Compare two ways to monitor noise near a school. Say which method is cheaper, which is more accurate, and what you recommend. Use because, so, although, and may/might/can.
